p.ALL-COMMITS-FOLLOW-THE-CONVENTIONAL-COMM: All commits in this project follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) specification.

p.this-document-is-the-shape-body-and-scop: This document is the message shape, body structure, and scope convention each commit must carry.

facts.HEADER-TARGET-LENGTH-AND-HARD-LIMIT: **Target length:** ≤ 60 characters. **Hard limit:** 72. Git web UIs truncate beyond that, and a truncated subject on the commit list is how decisions become invisible to readers who scan rather than scroll.
facts.HEADER-IMPERATIVE-MOOD: **Imperative mood.** "add", not "added"; "fix", not "fixes"; "refactor", not "refactored". The subject completes the sentence *"If applied, this commit will …"*.
facts.HEADER-LOWERCASE: **Lowercase.** Including the first word after the `type(scope):` prefix. The typed prefix is the visual anchor; a capitalised first word competes with it for attention.

td.fact: Bug fix. Name what broke and what it now does.
Build system, external dependency, toolchain pin.
Add or fix tests; no production-code change.
Revert a previous commit; reference the reverted SHA in the body.

p.TWO-TYPES-AT-ONCE-MEANS-TWO-COMMITS: If a commit feels like two types at once, it is two commits.

p.SCOPE-NAMES-THE-MOST-AFFECTED-SUBSYSTEM: Scope names the most affected subsystem — a crate, a package, a module, a documentation area.

p.the-narrower-form-hits-the-log-filter-co: `feat(wal): add morning routine` is better than `feat(core): add wal morning routine`, because readers filter the log by scope and the narrower form hits the filter correctly.

p.scope-is-optional-in-the-grammar-but-omi: Scope is optional in the strict Conventional Commits grammar, but omit it only when the change legitimately has no scope (e.g. a project-wide `.gitattributes` addition).

p.A-BLANK-LINE-AFTER-THE-SUBJECT-THEN-A-FR: A single blank line after the subject, then a free-form body.

facts.INCLUDE-WHY-THIS-CHANGE-WAS-MADE: **Why this change was made.** Link to the spec section, issue, measurement, or conversation that drove it. Use `spec://…` URIs so future sessions can follow the reference without having to guess where it is documented.
facts.INCLUDE-WHAT-FOLLOWS-FROM-IT: **What follows from it.** Consequences that are invisible in the diff: "this unblocks FEAT-007"; "after this, old callers must be migrated"; "this is a temporary workaround for #42".
facts.INCLUDE-WHAT-WAS-CONSIDERED-AND-REJECTED: **What was considered and rejected.** One line each. Future-you re-opens this conversation every six months unless the log says "we considered adaptive timeout and rejected it because of UX unpredictability".

facts.SKIP-WHAT-THE-DIFF-ALREADY-SHOWS: **Do not describe what the diff already shows.** "This commit adds a function `foo()`" is noise — the diff shows that. The message should answer "why did `foo()` need to exist?".
facts.SKIP-IMPLEMENTATION-DETAILS-THAT-WILL-CH: **Do not include implementation details that will change on the next refactor.** They rot faster than the surrounding prose and mislead readers once stale.

p.A-THREE-LINE-BODY-IS-FINE-FOR-A-SMALL-FI: A three-line body is fine for a small fix.

p.A-TWENTY-LINE-BODY-IS-FINE-FOR-A-MILESTO: A twenty-line body is fine for a milestone commit where the reasoning matters.

p.brevity-at-the-expense-of-the-why-costs-: Length is not a virtue, but brevity at the expense of the *why* is a cost paid on every future read.

p.PREFER-PARAGRAPHS-WHEN-THE-REASONING-IS-: Prefer paragraphs over bullet lists when the reasoning is continuous.

p.BULLETS-ARE-FOR-GENUINELY-PARALLEL-ITEMS: Bullets are for enumerations of genuinely parallel items — three rejected alternatives, four affected callers.

p.DO-NOT-BULLET-A-SINGLE-PARAGRAPH-OF-PROS: Do not bullet a single paragraph of prose into pieces.

example-small-fix.title: Small fix
example-small-fix.fence:
fix(wal): stop crashing on missing _Updated line
Treat a WAL without `_Updated:` as "age = infinite" rather than panicking. The guard previously short-circuited the whole status check, so stale-WAL projects could not run `vibe check`. Tested against an empty WAL and a WAL whose first line is a stray comment.

example-feature.title: Feature
example-feature.fence:
feat(registry): freshness TTL for cloned mirrors
Cache under ~/.vibe/registries/<hash>/ now carries a meta.toml with last_pulled_at. Pulls skip when the cache is fresher than the configured TTL (default 1 h); `vibe registry sync` forces a pull regardless. Rationale: every `vibe install` hitting the network was making offline work painful and slow.
Cited by spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/modules/vibe-registry/PROP-001#freshness.

example-refactor.title: Refactor
example-refactor.fence:
refactor(core): hoist timestamp helper out of vibe-cli
Both vibe-cli and vibe-registry needed `now_unix_utc`. Keeping it in vibe-cli forced vibe-registry to depend on the CLI crate, which violates the intended dependency direction. Moved to `vibe_core::timestamp`. No behaviour change; 78 tests still green.

example-revert.title: Revert
example-revert.fence:
revert: "feat(install): auto-retry on 429"
Reverts 1a2b3c4. The retry loop was masking real rate-limit bugs in the registry layer. Correct fix is to surface the 429 upstream and let the caller decide. Issue #47.

example-docs-sync.title: Docs sync (from sync-from-code flow)
example-docs-sync.fence:
docs(spec): sync timeout to 600s in PROP-003 §verification.timeout
Code changed TIMEOUT from 300 s to 600 s after VPN latency measurement (2026-03-05, 847 messages, 128 users). Spec now carries the new value, the reason, and the revisit trigger.

td.fact: Squash into the next real commit.
Name the bug and what drove the fix.
Two commits: refactor first, feature second.

p.CONVENTIONAL-COMMITS-DOES-NOT-ENFORCE-AT: Conventional Commits does not by itself enforce atomicity.

p.A-VALID-MESSAGE-CAN-STILL-VIOLATE-THE-AT: A commit with the subject `feat(core): add foo, bar, and baz` is syntactically valid Conventional Commits *and* a violation of the atomic rule. Both rules run together:

facts.BOTH-RULES-ONE-IDEA-PER-COMMIT: The commit carries exactly one idea (atomic).
facts.BOTH-RULES-THE-CONVENTIONAL-COMMITS-SHAP: The message announces that idea in the Conventional Commits shape (`type(scope): subject` + *why* body).

p.PASS-BOTH-AND-THE-COMMIT-IS-WELL-FORMED: Pass both, and the commit is well-formed.
